belief: I must be above others to be worthy, safe, or seen.
counterbelief: My worth is not dependent on rank; I can acknowledge others and still stand firmly.

belief: Someone else receiving goodness reduces what is possible for me.
counterbelief: Another person’s success does not cancel my possibility; I can contribute without losing myself.

belief: If I do not attack or punish, I lose power and will be harmed.
counterbelief: I can protect a boundary and respond forcefully without retaliating.

belief: My effort will not matter, or beginning will expose that I cannot succeed.
counterbelief: A small chosen action matters even before I know the final outcome.

belief: I am safe and valuable only if I keep more than enough—or spend to prove that I matter.
counterbelief: I can create safety through realistic stewardship while sharing from choice and enoughness.

belief: More consumption will finally fill the discomfort or emptiness I feel.
counterbelief: I can notice the actual need and choose sufficiency without denying ordinary pleasure.

belief: Being desired, possessing someone, or obtaining pleasure is what makes me worthy or complete.
counterbelief: Desire can be felt without ownership; intimacy requires mutuality, consent, and honest regard.
